# `OtaUpdate`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Updater (firmware 9.75): OTA session progress, failure, cancellation or completion.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | event (device sends) |
| Grade | PURE GETTER (observation only) |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ (firmware 9.75); 32-bit recipient rule unresolved |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.75, updater OTA manager NotifyUpdateEvent @0x313e0 and NotifyCompleteEvent @0x2ff20 (64-bit build); 32-bit build has the same strings |

Emitted by the updater's OTA manager on the TCP 4350 JSON server during an OTA session. Members appear in this order: state, stage (when the stage is not idle), module (when non-empty), code (when nonzero), error (when non-empty), then route (an empty array). state is working, fail or cancel. Completion is a separate form with state complete, main_version, need_reboot and route. It is sent only when an event server is set. Both the progress form and the completion form are broadcast: the 64-bit build passes no socket or requester address to the event server (firmware 9.75, READ), unlike Update, which is addressed to one client. Whether every retained event socket is eligible, and the 32-bit recipient rule, were not separately audited. This event is new in firmware 9.75; firmware 9.31 had no emitter. App 3.3.2 consumes it (state, stage, optional code and error, main_version, optional need_reboot); the firmware adds module and the cancel state. A pending receive whose binary connection does not arrive within 15 s fails with code 546 (ota module binary connection timeout; firmware 9.75, 64-bit, READ). When the completion form has need_reboot true the device schedules a reboot 2 s later (READ, 64-bit).

Side effects: Observation only for the receiver.

## Request params

None. Events are sent by the device without a request; the payload is below.

## Payload

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Event` | string | yes | - | Discriminator. Fixed value `"OtaUpdate"`. [READ] |
| `Timestamp` | string | yes | - | Decimal string <seconds>.<nine digits> (as other updater events). [READ] |
| `state` | string | yes | - | working, fail, cancel, or complete for the completion form. One of: `working`, `fail`, `cancel`, `complete`. [READ] |
| `stage` | string | if stage is not idle (progress form) | - | OTA stage name (see ota_get_session). One of: `pending`, `receiving`, `upgrading`, `complete`, `fail`. [READ] |
| `module` | string | if non-empty | - | Module concerned. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | if nonzero | - | Failure code (546 for a pending-receive timeout, firmware 9.75; other values in the error table of the updater chapter). [READ] |
| `error` | string | if non-empty | - | Failure text. [READ] |
| `main_version` | string | if state is complete | - | Main version now installed. [READ] |
| `need_reboot` | boolean | if state is complete | - | true when the device reboots after the upgrade. [READ] |
| `route` | array<string> | yes | - | Always an empty array. [READ] |

## Errors

None. Failures appear in the payload (`code`, `error`) when `state` is `fail`.

## Example

Event, working - Shape READ; values invented:

```json
{"Event":"OtaUpdate","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","state":"working","stage":"receiving","module":"example_module","route":[]}
```

Event, complete - Shape READ; values invented:

```json
{"Event":"OtaUpdate","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","state":"complete","main_version":"9.99","need_reboot":true,"route":[]}
```
